articles.title: Why Do Onions Make Us Cry?
articles.dek: You are not sad, but the tears keep coming. What is the onion doing?

sources.name: Britannica: Why do onions make you cry?
Discover Magazine: Why do onions make us cry?

paras: You are helping in the kitchen. Your mum asks you to cut an onion. After a minute, your eyes start to hurt. Then tears run down your face. You are not sad, so why are you crying? Let's find the answer step by step.

An onion looks simple, but it is full of tiny cells. Inside these cells, there are special chemicals. They stay in different parts of each cell. When the onion is whole, they never meet. So a whole onion on the table can't hurt your eyes.

Everything changes when you cut it. The knife breaks the cells, and the chemicals mix. Very quickly, they make a new chemical. It is a kind of gas, and it goes up into the air. If you cut an onion, this gas will reach your face in a few seconds.

Your eyes don't like this gas at all. It touches the front of your eyes and makes them sting. Your eyes want to protect themselves. So they make lots of tears. The tears wash the gas away. Crying is your body's way to keep your eyes safe.

Why do onions do this? Scientists think it helps the plant. An onion grows under the ground. Small animals sometimes want to eat it. If an animal bites an onion, the gas will hurt its eyes and mouth. Then it will probably leave the onion alone!

Can you stop the tears? Here are some easy tips. If you put the onion in the fridge for half an hour first, you will cry less. Cold makes the chemicals slow. Use a sharp knife, too. A sharp knife breaks fewer cells than an old one. If you open a window, the gas will go away faster.
Cooking changes onions as well. When you cook them, the strong smell goes away. They become soft and sweet. So next time you cry in the kitchen, don't worry. It's only science!

articles.title: Which Club Did You Join?
articles.dek: Cooking, chess or photos? Three students tell us about their new after-school club.
paras: This term, our school started six new after-school clubs. They meet on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4 to 5:30. We asked three students: Which club did you choose, and why?

Mia, 13: I chose the cooking club. I love making things for my family, but at home I usually just watch my dad. In the club, we learn to cook easy meals. Last week, we made vegetable soup. My little brother doesn't enjoy eating vegetables, but he finished my soup! Next month, I hope to cook dinner for my parents. It will be a surprise.

Daniel, 14: I wanted to join the football club, but it was already full. So I decided to try the chess club. At first, I didn't want to go. I thought chess was boring and slow. I was wrong! Now I really enjoy playing it! Our teacher, Mr Patel, is very patient. He keeps showing us clever new moves. In spring, we're going to enter a competition in the city. I can't wait!

Aiko, 12: I joined the photography club. I'm a bit shy, and I don't like talking in front of a lot of people. I wanted to find a quiet hobby. Every week, we walk around the school and take photos of trees, birds and people. Our teacher taught us to use the light well. I'd like to have my own camera one day. For now, I borrow one from the club.
So, who is happiest? All three students say the same thing. They have learned new skills, and they have made new friends. Which club would you like to join?

articles.title: My First Climbing Lesson
articles.dek: Leo tries to climb a twelve-metre wall. Will he get to the top?
paras: Hi everyone! It's Leo again. On Saturday, I did something new. I went to a climbing centre which opened last month near my school. My cousin Sofia, who climbs every week, came with me.

The centre has a huge wall that is twelve metres high. It is covered in small coloured holds. A hold is a little piece that you put your hands and feet on. Each colour shows a different route up the wall. The easy routes are green, and the hard ones are black.

First, we met our teacher, Kenji. He is the man who checks everyone's ropes. He gave me a harness. A harness is a kind of belt that goes around your waist and legs. Kenji showed me how to put it on. Then he tied the rope to it. He said, 'Always check your knot before you climb.'

My first climb was on a green route. I got to the middle, and then I looked down. Big mistake! My legs started to shake. Sofia shouted, 'Don't look down! Look for the next hold!' I listened to her. Slowly, I reached the top and touched the bell which hangs there. Ding!
Coming down was the best part. You sit back in your harness. Then the person who holds your rope lets you down slowly. It feels a bit like flying.
After two hours, my arms were really tired. My hands were red, too. But I wasn't sad at all. I was proud of myself.

Sofia gave me a tip that I want to share with you. Use your legs, not only your arms. Your legs are much stronger! I'm going to go back next Saturday, and I want to try a blue route. Have you ever tried climbing? Tell me in the comments!

items.why: A ball is a thing, so use which.

items.q: I have a friend ___ plays tennis every day.
items.why: That can be used for a person, like who.

items.q: The girl ___ won the race is in my class.
items.why: The girl is a person, so use who or that.

items.q: We played in the park ___ is next to the river.
items.why: The park is a place, so use which or that.

items.q: A goalkeeper is a player ___ stops the ball.
items.why: A player is a person, so use who or that.

kps.fact: Leo looked down and his legs started to shake.

mindmap.question: What happened at Leo's first climbing lesson?

summary.intro: Leo writes about his first climbing lesson.
summary.model: Leo was scared in the middle of the wall, but Sofia helped him. He reached the top, so he felt proud.

options.t: Leo went to a new climbing centre with his cousin Sofia.
options.why: This is the start of the blog.
options.evidence: I went to a climbing centre which opened last month near my school.

options.t: He was scared on the wall, but he reached the top.
options.evidence: Slowly, I reached the top and touched the bell which hangs there.

options.t: He felt proud and wants to go back next week.
options.evidence: I'm going to go back next Saturday

options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: The easy routes are green, and the hard ones are black.

Leo's first climb was on a black route.

options.evidence: My first climb was on a green route.

Say how the story ended and how you felt.
